title: Piecewise and Step Functions

key_big: First decide which piece the input belongs to.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A piecewise function uses different rules on different parts of the domain. First decide which piece the input belongs to.
  • At a boundary, check the signs: < and > leave the point out, ≤ and ≥ include it.
  • The greatest integer function ⌊x⌋ rounds down: ⌊3.7⌋ = 3 and ⌊−2.3⌋ = −3. Its graph looks like steps.
  • A piecewise function is continuous at a boundary when both pieces give the same value there.

Examples

Example

f(x) = 2x + 1 if x < 3, x2 if x ≥ 3; find f(3)

3 ≥ 3, so use x2

Answer: f(3) = 9

Example

Parking: $4 the first hour, $2 each extra hour or part; 3.2 hours

2.2 extra hours → 3 parts

Answer: $4 + 3 × $2 = $10

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong piece at the boundaryLook at ≤ and < carefully.
⌊−2.3⌋ = −2Round down: −3.
Rounding a part of an hour downA part counts as a whole step.
